title: ?qa=1 ships a full remote-control + cheat + answer-key bridge to production
evidence: `const QA_ON = /[?&]qa=1(?:&|$)/.test(location.search);` (25684). When true it exposes `window.QA = { cmd, boot, catalog, answerData };   // console access too` (25891). Commands include `forceWin()` — `bfState.bossHP = 0; bossWin();` (25775); `unlockAll()` — `player.level = Math.max(player.level, 20); player.shells = Math.max(player.shells, 100000);` (25829); `maxProgress()` (25838); `setState({coins,xp,level,rank})` (25817); `level(n)`, `lesson(key)`, `resetProgress()`. Worst is `answerData(id, diff)` (25746), which returns `out.correctAnswer = st.answer` and `out.validation = g.validate ? fnSrc(g.validate)` — the correct answer AND the validator source for every registered mini-game. ?qa=1 also bypasses the progress-wipe prompt at 1683 (`|| _qa ||`) and paints the internal BUILD_TAG at 24114.
risk: A tester who is handed, or guesses, `playchartquest.com/play.html?qa=1` gets: the answer key to the entire educational library dumped from the console, 100,000 shells, level 20, every boss and lesson unlocked, and one-call boss wins. The IP loss is the answer key — that is the teachable content the courses are meant to sell. The analytics loss is worse: `forceWin()` calls the real `bossWin()`, which CQTrack wraps at 27751 to emit `boss_defeated`, and `QAboss()` calls the real `openBoss()` (wrapped at 27745) to emit `boss_started`. Both are in ONCE (27459), so the fabricated events are recorded permanently and that tester's genuine boss events are silently discarded forever by `if (get(k)) return false;` (27618). The funnel cannot be repaired after the fact — the real event was never sent.
fix:
Gate the whole bridge on a dev check. Add one constant beside `_CQ_MUTE` (~line 1643, above the ?fresh block so it survives the query-string strip):

```js
const _CQ_DEV = (function () { try { var h = location.hostname;
  return location.protocol === 'file:' || h === 'localhost' || h === '127.0.0.1' || h === '::1'
    || /^192\.168\./.test(h) || /^10\./.test(h) || /^172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\./.test(h)
    || localStorage.getItem('cq_dev') === '1'; } catch (e) { return false; } })();
window._CQ_DEV = _CQ_DEV;   // the QA bridge is in a later <script> block
```

Then change 25684 to `const QA_ON = !!window._CQ_DEV && /[?&]qa=1(?:&|$)/.test(location.search);`. Nothing else in the bridge needs touching — every capability, `window.QA`, the postMessage listener (25880 `if (!QA_ON) return;`) and the BUILD_TAG paint already key off QA_ON or the same flag.
maintainabilityCost: Effectively zero for the daily loop. `scripts/cq.sh qr` builds `http://$IP:$P/chart-quest.html?fresh=1&mute=1` from `ipconfig getifaddr en0` (cq.sh:69) — a 192.168.x/10.x address — so every existing QR, `cq.sh serve`, file:// opens and the headless-Chrome iframe harness all satisfy _CQ_DEV unchanged. Testing ?qa=1 against the LIVE site needs `localStorage.cq_dev='1'` typed once per device in devtools; it is sticky forever after. No build step, no change to cq.sh, verify.js, the byte-identity contract or the deploy. The one real cost: if you ever debug on a production URL from a device you have not unlocked, the flags appear dead — mitigate with a one-line console.info when _CQ_DEV is false and a dev flag was passed.

verified.correction:
Finding is real; downgrade Critical -> High, keep QUICK_WIN. Four corrections:

1. REACHABILITY IS NARROWER THAN STATED — and the project's own standard link neuters it. chart-quest.html:1697 does `_p.delete('fresh'); _p.delete('qa');` then `history.replaceState(...)` inside the top-level ?fresh block, which executes at parse time, long before QA_ON is evaluated at :25684. So `?fresh=1&qa=1` leaves QA_ON FALSE — the bridge is dead. Per the project's beginner-mode-testing rule every tester URL carries ?fresh=1, and cq.sh:69 hard-codes `?fresh=1&mute=1`. Only a BARE `?qa=1` (no fresh) arms the bridge. The cited "playchartquest.com/play.html?qa=1" is also mechanically imprecise: play.html contains zero QA code (`grep -c "qa=1" website/play.html` = 0); it works only because play.html:148 forwards location.search into the iframe. `game.html?qa=1` is the direct path.

2. THE ANSWER-KEY "IP LOSS" IS ~ENTIRELY ALREADY PUBLIC. There is no build step: website/game.html is 1.87 MB of unminified, commented source containing every MG.REG entry with its `gen` and `validate` functions inline. `answerData()` is a convenience wrapper over content already fully readable in view-source. The marginal exposure is convenience, not disclosure. It still matters under "reduce casual copying" (a URL flag is the casual path), but "the answer key to the entire educational library" overstates what an attacker gains beyond Ctrl-U.

3. THE CHEATS ADD LITTLE OVER DEVTOOLS. Progress is client-side localStorage only (the beta tables are RLS-gated, write-only via edge function, analytics only). `unlockAll()` setting `player.shells = 100000` is something any visitor can already do by editing localStorage on a fully-readable client-side game. No server-authoritative state is affected.

4. "PERMANENTLY / CANNOT BE REPAIRED" IS FALSE. The ONCE stamps are `cq_bt_*` keys and the player id is `cq_pid` (:27473). chart-quest.html:1686 `_rk.forEach(k => { if (/^(cq_|shellTrade)/.test(k)) localStorage.removeItem(k); });` wipes BOTH on any ?fresh load — the standard tester link. `CQTrack.reset()` (:27847-27852) also clears every `cq_bt_*` stamp explicitly. So a poisoned device self-heals on the next ?fresh visit. The residual harm is real but is FUNNEL NOISE, not loss: the fabricated boss_started/boss_defeated land under a player_id that is then discarded, so the beta funnel shows one phantom boss-defeating player rather than losing a genuine event. This is the one harm devtools alone would not casually cause, and it is the strongest remaining argument for the fix.

The proposed one-line fix is sound and I found nothing it breaks: dashboard.html does not deploy, the postMessage listener already returns on `if (!QA_ON) return;` (:25880) and additionally checks `ev.origin !== location.origin`, the game's own same-origin iframe is unaffected (no header/CSP change involved), and the fix is a pure source edit that flows through cq.sh mirror/site with the verify.js #8 byte-identity gate intact. Use `window._CQ_DEV` as proposed — the bridge is in a later <script> block and top-level const is not a window property (the Block-2 script-scope trap). One addition to the fix: also gate the BUILD_TAG paint at :24114, which tests `location.search` independently of QA_ON and still leaks the internal build string on production via `?build=1`.

title: window.CQTrack.event() and .survey() let anyone write arbitrary rows into the live beta tables from the console
evidence: `window.CQTrack = { event: event, crash: crash, flush: ..., survey: function (row) {...}, stampCompleted: function () { set('cq_bt_beta_completed', String(Date.now())); }, pid: pid, ... reset: ... };` (27821-27855). The complete accepted vocabulary sits three lines above it in plain text: `var NAMES = ['session_start','session_end','return_visit','tutorial_started',... 'beta_completed','survey_started','survey_submitted','crash'];` (27453-27456). `survey()` derives `r.response_id = r.response_id || ('r-' + pid());`, and `CQTrack.reset()` (27851) clears every cq_bt_* flag.
risk: `CQTrack.event('beta_completed',{})` from any console writes a real row. Repeated `CQTrack.reset()` plus rewriting `localStorage.cq_pid` allows an arbitrary number of fabricated testers and survey responses. This is not a likely act of malice from 10-20 invited friends, but it is the kind of thing one bored tester does for fun, and at n=20 a handful of injected rows moves every percentage in the Founder Report. Note the real enforcement point is the beta-ingest edge function's validation and its stated 120 req/min budget (cq-track.js:297) — that is outside this area but is where the durable control belongs.
fix: Do not remove the API — CQBeta and the survey page depend on it. Narrow the surface instead: drop `stampCompleted` and `reset` from the published object unless `_CQ_DEV` (they are only ever called by CQBeta and by hand), and treat server-side validation in supabase/functions/beta-ingest as the real control. If you want a cheap client-side signal, have `event()` attach `props._dev = true` whenever `_CQ_DEV` is set, so every event produced on a dev machine is filterable in the report.
maintainabilityCost: Low. Keeping `event`/`crash`/`flush`/`survey`/`pid`/`state` published preserves all debugging; you lose the ability to type `CQTrack.reset()` on a production device without the unlock key. The `_dev` prop is a genuine improvement — it lets the Founder Report exclude the founder's own dozens of test runs, which right now are indistinguishable from real testers.

title: ?flow=1 ships an explicitly unvalidated gameplay prototype to external testers
evidence: The block header says it outright: "GATED OFF by default — enable for testing with ?flow=1 (or localStorage cq_flow='1'). Normal play is completely unaffected until this is validated on a device." (14732-14733). The flag: `const FLOW_READS = (function(){ try { return new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('flow') === '1' || localStorage.getItem('cq_flow') === '1'; } catch(e){ return false; } })();` (14734). It rewires the movement keys — `flowReadCommit(0)` on ArrowUp/KeyW and `flowReadCommit(1)` on ArrowDown/KeyS (6780-6781) — and awards shells on a correct read.
risk: A tester on ?flow=1 plays a different game from every other tester: an unvalidated mechanic that changes what jump and tuck mean and pays out shells. Their qualitative survey feedback would be about a prototype the founder is not shipping, which is worse than no feedback — it is feedback that reads as real. This is the classic case of a prototype flag surviving into a release because it was correctly gated off and therefore never noticed again.
fix: `return _CQ_DEV && (new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('flow') === '1' || localStorage.getItem('cq_flow') === '1');` at 14734. The localStorage half matters here too — `cq_flow` is a plain key anyone can set, and unlike the URL flag it is sticky.
maintainabilityCost: None. The flag exists solely to validate the mechanic on the founder's own device, which is exactly what _CQ_DEV permits.

title: ?jtut re-runs the Journal onboarding over real progress, ignoring the once-ever flag
evidence: `window._CQ_JTUT = (function () { try { return /[?&]jtut(=|&|$)/.test(location.search); } ... })();` (1656), auto-firing `API.devStart()` on load (27383-27384). devStart is `if (S.active) return false; reset(); waitThenBegin({ dev: true }); return true;` (27279-27284) — it calls `reset()` first, so it deliberately discards the completion flag. title: ?reach paints the internal level-design telemetry overlay over the live game
evidence: `const _REACH_DEBUG = (function () { try { return /[?&]reach(=|&|$)/.test(location.search); } ... })();` (1649). The overlay it enables draws "red hatch = unsafe: inside terrain, or below the chart baseline (dead space) / amber line = the playable ceiling / per-shell tick + clearance readout / live spawn accept/reject tally with the reason each candidate died" (18185-18188). The comment at 18189 asserts "Gated on the query string only — see _REACH_DEBUG. Players can never see this" — which is precisely the assumption this finding contradicts, since the query string is player-supplied. It also gates a console warning: `if (_viol.length && _REACH_DEBUG) console.warn('[CQREACH] healed', _viol);` (16234).
risk: No cheating, no analytics corruption. It exposes the collectible-placement solver's internals — the reachability envelope, the spawn accept/reject reasons — which is design IP, and a tester who lands on it sees what looks like a broken, half-finished build. Minor on both counts, but it is a one-word change to fix.
fix: `const _REACH_DEBUG = _CQ_DEV && /[?&]reach(=|&|$)/.test(location.search);` at 1649. Note _CQ_DEV must be declared above this line — it belongs at the top of the same capture block beside _CQ_MUTE, above the ?fresh query-strip, for exactly the reason the existing comments give.
maintainabilityCost: None. The standard beginner-mode test link is documented at 1647 as `?fresh=1&mute=1&reach=1` on a LAN URL, which satisfies _CQ_DEV.

title: BUILD_TAG is a 700-character internal engineering changelog, rendered on-canvas by ?qa=1 or ?build=1
evidence: `const BUILD_TAG = 'build 334 - BOOT-CRASH CAPTURE. CQTrack installs its error listeners inside boot(), deferred to DOMContentLoaded, and in this file that block is around line 27,400 of 28,100 ... Zero crash rows in 118 events was not evidence of no crashes, it was evidence we could not see them. ...';` (2986). Rendered by `if (/[?&](qa|build)=1/.test(location.search))` (24114), under a comment that already states the intent: "BUILD TAG — QA ONLY (Phase-1 polish: never show players an internal build string)."
risk: The string discloses internal beta volume (118 events), the analytics architecture, file line numbers and the reasoning behind a recent bug — and it is in the deployed source in plaintext regardless of the flag, so gating the flag does not hide it. Rating this Low because the exposure is the string, not the flag; the flag only makes it visible without devtools. Worth noting because the founder's stated goal includes preventing accidental exposure, and 'zero crash rows in 118 events' is a private beta metric.
fix: Two independent changes. (1) Gate the paint: `if (_CQ_DEV && /[?&](qa|build)=1/.test(location.search))` at 24114. (2) The real fix — split the constant: keep a short machine-readable `const BUILD_TAG = 'build 334';` for the cache/QR identity check (which is what `scripts/cq.sh qr` greps for at cq.sh:76, `grep "BUILD_TAG =" ... grep -oE "build [0-9]+"`) and move the prose to a separate `BUILD_NOTES` comment that is not a rendered string.
maintainabilityCost: The split needs care: cq.sh:76 and cq.sh:79 both parse the BUILD_TAG line, and the guard compares disk against wire. Keeping the `BUILD_TAG = 'build NNN'` prefix intact means neither line changes. Real cost is the habit change — the founder currently writes the build story into the constant, and that story is genuinely useful; it just needs to live in the comment directly above rather than inside the string.

title: No gate enforces dev-flag hygiene, so the next debug hook will ship the same way these twelve did
evidence: verify.js already runs exactly this class of enforcement — `// 12 — CANDLE-LANGUAGE GATE (build 287). The enforcement wire the Visual Market Constitution promised` (221), `// 13 — window.CQ OWNER-INTEGRITY GATE` (236), `// 14 — COLLECTIBLE LAW 001 GATE` (251), `// 15 — LESSON-LABEL GATE` (267), `// 16 — MARKET IDENTITY GATE` (283). There is no equivalent for debug flags, which is why ten of them accumulated undetected across builds 233-334.
risk: Every finding above is a one-line fix, and every one of them will regress. The pattern in this codebase is well established: a flag is added correctly gated-off for a legitimate test, the comment says 'players never pass it', and it is never revisited. Without a gate, the audit has to be re-run by hand before every release.
fix: Add check #17 to scripts/verify.js: scan chart-quest.html for every `location.search` / `URLSearchParams` test, and FAIL unless each match is either on a short allowlist (`mute`, `fresh`) or appears on a line containing `_CQ_DEV`. About 20 lines, matching the structure of #12-#16. It runs inside `cq.sh ship` (cq.sh:51, `"$0" mirror && node scripts/verify.js && "$0" site`), so it blocks the deploy rather than nagging.
maintainabilityCost: Real but modest and the same cost the five existing gates already carry: adding a genuinely new player-facing URL parameter means editing the allowlist, and a regex gate can false-fail on an unusual formatting of the same test. Given that this exact failure mode has now produced ten live findings, the gate pays for itself on the first prevented regression. Do NOT extend this into a build step — the whole point is that it validates the readable source in place and leaves chart-quest.html byte-identical to website/game.html, preserving verify.js check #8.

title: 590 KB (30.9%) of the deployed game is developer comments — including 50 verbatim founder quotes and written post-mortems of shipped defects
evidence: Measured over the deployed file: 4,719 line comments (330,903 B), 719 block comments (255,147 B), 29 HTML comments (4,148 B) = 590,198 B of 1,913,088 B (30.9%). Gzip: 616,169 B → 362,680 B stripped. 50 comments are tagged `FOUNDER`. Representative content: `/* FOUNDER (build 317) — THIS WAS THE ACTUAL "WEIRD GLITCHY SCREEN SHAKE". ... It was never a stylistic choice; it was a CSS bug, and it hit the wrong-answer shake and the victory shake too */` (:460-466); `/* FOUNDER (build 320) — THIS IS WHY THE TRADE STILL ENDED EARLY ... trade._press is never initialised anywhere ... so `!trade._press` evaluated `!undefined === true` */` (:5212-5214); `/* A HIDDEN PAGE HAS NO SIZE ... That left the game running on broken geometry, and since build 313 it is also visible as a flood of GROUND_NOT_READY spawn rejections — collectibles silently refused for the rest of the session. */` (:3029-3031); `/* FOUNDER (build 313) — "I don't see any of the destructible boxes in level 1, we should have 2." */` (:5924); `/* T-001 · WICK LAW (FOUNDER REJECTION #2 — "there are far too many wicks") */` (:5439).
risk: Three things at once. (a) A tester reading source gets a running list of the game's known defects and the exact conditions that trigger them — useful for a bug report, corrosive in a screenshot. (b) The founder's unfiltered product criticism of his own build is published under his own domain. (c) It is 248 KB of gzipped payload on a mobile-first game whose funnel already leaks before the first trade. The perf argument alone justifies the fix independent of any IP argument.
fix: LINE-PRESERVING comment strip at the deploy copy only. Add scripts/strip_comments.js using acorn 8.15.0 (already at node_modules/acorn as a transitive dep of javascript-obfuscator — promote it to an explicit devDependency so it survives a prune): parse each inline <script> body with `onComment`, and replace each comment's source range with the SAME NUMBER of newlines rather than deleting it; do the same for `<!-- -->` and CSS `/* */`. Then change cq.sh:37 from `cp chart-quest.html website/game.html` to `node scripts/strip_comments.js chart-quest.html website/game.html`. I measured the exact output: 1,324,538 B raw (-30.7%), 363,373 B gzip (-41%), and line count EXACTLY 28,292 — identical to chart-quest.html. Block extraction is safe: `</script` occurs exactly 9 times in the file, matching the 9 real closing tags, so none is hidden inside a string.
maintainabilityCost: Low, and deliberately so. The dev loop is untouched: you still open, edit and debug chart-quest.html with every comment intact, and `cq.sh serve` / the QR test URL are unaffected. Production debuggability is preserved by the line-preserving trick — a stack trace at line N in the deployed file is line N in chart-quest.html, no source map needed, which is the specific thing minification would take away. The real ongoing costs are: (i) `cq.sh site`'s build-tag check at cq.sh:47 now greps a transformed file — it reads the BUILD_TAG string literal, which survives, but verify this on the first run; (ii) one new script to maintain; (iii) `diff chart-quest.html website/game.html` stops being empty, so if anything downstream assumes byte-identity to the site copy it must be updated — I found nothing that does (verify.js reads only chart-quest.html and index.html, verify.js:29-30). Do NOT hand-roll a character-scanner version of this; use acorn, so regex literals and template strings are handled by a parser rather than by luck.

title: BUILD_TAG is a runtime string that publishes the beta's telemetry blind spot and crash history — and no code transform will remove it
evidence: `const BUILD_TAG = 'build 334 - BOOT-CRASH CAPTURE. CQTrack installs its error listeners inside boot(), deferred to DOMContentLoaded, and in this file that block is around line 27,400 of 28,100 - so the one failure that matters most, a parse-time throw that white-screens the page, was structurally unrecordable. Zero crash rows in 118 events was not evidence of no crashes, it was evidence we could not see them. A tiny dependency-free listener now sits in the HEAD ... and if CQTrack never boots at all it posts the crash itself after 8 seconds. Deliberately placed far above the CQTRACK markers so the sync gate is unaffected.';` — a single ~700-character string literal.
risk: It states the sample size (118 events), admits the beta was blind to its own crashes, and describes exactly where the telemetry listeners sit and how to defeat the sync gate. Unlike the comments, this is a live string: it is `grep`-able in the deployed file, survives comment stripping, survives minification, and survives obfuscation's stringArray in decodable form. cq.sh:47 greps it, so it cannot simply be deleted. It is the clearest case in this area of "the transform question is a distraction from the content question".
fix: Split the field. Keep `BUILD_TAG = 'build 334'` — that is all cq.sh:47's `grep -o "build [0-9][^']*"` and the cache-check playtest workflow actually need. Move the narrative into a comment directly above it (where the stripper then removes it from the deploy) or into the commit message, which is where the other 333 builds' rationale already lives. Apply the same rule going forward: BUILD_TAG is a version, not a changelog.
maintainabilityCost: None. The cache-check workflow is unchanged — a tester still reads "build 334" to confirm which build loaded. It is strictly less to type per release.

title: Unwired-checkout stub names the payment providers and tells the reader payment is not real
evidence: `function cqStartCheckout(ov, onLater) { // FOUNDER HOOK: wire a real checkout here. Set window.CQ_CHECKOUT_URL to your` / `// hosted checkout (Stripe / Gumroad / Lemon Squeezy / Paddle) and it opens there.` / `try { if (window.CQ_CHECKOUT_URL) { window.open(window.CQ_CHECKOUT_URL, '_blank'); return; } } catch (e) {}` (:13820-13823). The user-visible fallback copy at :13831 reads "Payment isn't wired into this build yet."
risk: Two layers. The comment is removable and should go. The `window.CQ_CHECKOUT_URL` global is not a comment — it is a documented, globally writable redirect target: anything that can run script on the page (a future third-party include, a compromised dependency) can set it and `window.open` an arbitrary URL from a trusted flow the user reached by clicking a buy button. Combined with courses.html shipping $39.99/$149.99 for products that do not exist, a tester reading source learns the pricing is aspirational before the founder gets to frame it.
fix: Two small changes. (1) Let the stripper remove the provider-naming comment (covered by the F3 fix). (2) Validate before opening: require the URL to parse, be `https:`, and match a hardcoded host allowlist, rather than opening whatever the global holds. Leave the visible "Payment isn't wired" copy alone — it is honest and player-facing, and honesty about the beta is worth more than the concealment.
maintainabilityCost: Negligible; ~5 lines, and the hook still works exactly as designed when the real checkout is wired.

title: The dev/test backdoors are documented in the deployed source, in prose

The exposure is that the comments are a step-by-step guide to skipping the tutorial, wiping a save, and marking the beta complete without playing. title: Minifying the game would cost line-accurate production debugging and buy almost nothing over stripping — recommend against it, for now
evidence: Measured deltas from the deployed 1,913,088 B / 616,169 B gzip baseline: comment strip alone gives 1,324,538 B / 363,373 B gzip at an IDENTICAL 28,292 lines. The remaining code after stripping is ~1.32 MB, of which 216,673 B (11.3% of the original file) is string literals ≥25 chars — content a minifier cannot shrink. The file is one 1.87 MB HTML document with 8 inline <script> blocks that share global lexical bindings by bare name across block boundaries (game.html:26357: `<script>, so they are GLOBAL LEXICAL bindings — shared with this block by BARE NAME but ...`), which is hostile to every bundler and makes cross-block mangling unsafe by construction.
risk: This is the cost side of the central question, stated plainly. Minifying adds maybe 15-20% more over-the-wire on top of the 41% stripping already gives, and in exchange: (a) production stack traces stop mapping to chart-quest.html line numbers, and there are no source maps because there is no build that could emit them — so the boot-crash telemetry the founder JUST built at :2986 to see white-screens would start reporting mangled, unlocatable frames; (b) cross-block bare-name sharing means a mangler must be configured to not rename top-level bindings, which removes most of its benefit anyway; (c) it adds a second, slower, failure-prone stage to a ship command that currently takes seconds.
fix: Recommend AGAINST minification and obfuscation. Ship the line-preserving comment strip (F3) and stop there. Revisit only if two things become true at once: the file drops below ~1 MB, and a real error-reporting service with source-map upload is in place. Until then the honest answer is: not worth it yet, and the 41% gzip win from stripping already captures most of the available benefit at none of the debuggability cost.
maintainabilityCost: Recommending against it has zero cost. Recommending FOR it would cost the daily loop a slower ship, an extra tool to keep working, and — the one that actually matters for a solo founder — the ability to read a production stack trace and jump straight to the line in the source file he is already editing.

title: website/sw.js is a JavaScript syntax error — service worker never registers, and it is the only console error every tester sees
evidence: Line 16 closes the block comment: "the play page. That IS the desktop lag fix, so it must actually reach returning testers. */" — and then lines 17-18 are bare English prose sitting in executable scope: "   v10: the tracker itself changed (one session per visit, durable retry, build tag). cq-track.js" / "   is now precached EXPLICITLY rather than only runtime-cached, so it is unambiguously versioned. */". Proven, not inferred: `node --check website/sw.js` returns "SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'tracker'" pointing at line 17. The file is registered from three separate places, so this fires on every deployed page — website/index.html:2139 "navigator.serviceWorker.register('sw.js').catch(function(){});", website/assets/site.js:149 (identical line, loaded by every site page), and website/game.html:24143 "navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js').then(reg => { try { reg.update(); } catch (e) {} }).catch(() => {});".
risk: Two distinct costs. (1) Console: the `.catch(){}` swallows the promise rejection but not the browser's own report — per the SW spec, registration rejects on script evaluation failure and browsers log that parse error to the page console. This is the single line of console output a tester will actually see on a normal run, and it reads as "this site is broken". I could not confirm the exact browser wording because the rules forbid me driving a browser; the syntax error and the failed registration are proven from the file itself. (2) Functional: `const CACHE = 'chartquest-site-v12'` (line 19) never installs, so nothing is precached, `offline.html` never serves, and the freshness reload at game.html:24149-24152 can never fire because `controllerchange` requires a working worker — meaning the documented "I deployed but my phone shows the old version" fix is inoperative for the 10-20 invited testers.
fix: Move the `*/` from the end of line 16 to the end of line 18, or delete lines 17-18. One-character-class edit, no behaviour change beyond making the file parse. Verify with `node --check website/sw.js` before shipping. Note that sw.js lives in the output dir so it deploys directly; no mirror sync needed.
maintainabilityCost: None. This is a comment-delimiter repair, not a change to any system.

Two corrections to the risk framing; the defect and the fix stand as written.

title: verify.js syntax gate #3a only parses chart-quest.html's inline scripts — no standalone deployed .js file is ever syntax-checked

Add a check that runs the same `node --check` over an explicit list — website/sw.js and website/assets/{site,config,cq-track,market-data}.js — and `add('3c', 'Deployed standalone JS parses', ...)`. Roughly 10 lines using the existing `add`/`exists` helpers at verify.js:33-35. maintainabilityCost: Near zero: adds well under a second to `cq.sh ship`, touches no game code, and needs editing only when a new standalone JS file is added to the deploy — which is rare (five files today).

title: The only console-error gate (check #3b) is permanently inert and reports SKIP, which reads as a pass
evidence: "try { puppeteer = require('puppeteer'); } catch { add('3b', 'Headless boot (console errors)', 'SKIP', 'puppeteer not installed — `npm i -D puppeteer` to enable; syntax (3a) is the proxy'); return; }". title: access-control-allow-origin: * on every response lets any site read the full game source in-browser
evidence: Established production header set is `x-content-type-options`, `referrer-policy` and `access-control-allow-origin: *` only. risk: Any third-party page can `fetch('https://playchartquest.com/game.html').then(r=>r.text())` and read, re-host, diff or mine the entire commented source from a visitor's browser, with no server of their own. It does not stop a determined copier (curl works regardless), but it removes the last speed bump for drive-by, in-page scraping and for tooling that re-serves the source under another brand — which is exactly the 'casual copying' tier the founder asked about. Nothing on the site needs it: no cross-origin fetch exists, iframes do not require CORS, and the same-origin `new Audio()` with `a.crossOrigin = 'anonymous'` (game.html:23419) still passes the CORS check because same-origin responses always do.

If it survives, Cloudflare is stamping it downstream of `_headers` and the removal must be done with a dashboard Transform Rule instead. Deployment risk if it silently over-applies: essentially zero, because nothing cross-origin exists to break — but confirm the Supabase edge functions still accept the beta telemetry, since those set their OWN CORS headers on their own responses and are unaffected by this change.
maintainabilityCost: None today. One future gotcha: if the marketing site is ever split to a different domain from the game, or a partner is given an embed, this line must be revisited. Worth a one-line comment in _headers saying so.

title: Cache strategy is undeclared and about to become two-layered the moment sw.js is fixed
evidence: `/* BUMP THIS IN THE SAME COMMIT AS ANY CHANGE TO A PRECACHED OR RUNTIME-CACHED ASSET.` / `   Static assets below are cache-first with NO revalidation, so a returning tester keeps the` / `   old copy until this string changes.` (sw.js:10-12), `const CACHE = 'chartquest-site-v12';` (sw.js:19). The cache-first branch is sw.js:76-85: `caches.match(req).then(hit => hit || fetch(req)...)`. No `Cache-Control` is set anywhere in the repo for the deployed site — no website/_headers exists. Every asset is unhashed: `./assets/site.css`, `./assets/site.js`, `./assets/config.js`, `./assets/cq-track.js` (sw.js:24) keep the same filename across every build.
risk: Two failure modes. (1) TODAY: HTTP caching is entirely at Cloudflare's default with nothing pinning it, so a platform default change — or anyone adding a well-meaning `max-age=31536000` to the unhashed asset dirs — would pin testers to a stale build with no cache-busting mechanism available, because the filenames never change. (2) THE DAY sw.js IS FIXED (finding 1): the cache-first layer switches on for the first time and site.js/config.js/cq-track.js become pinned until `CACHE` is bumped by hand. config.js is the file that gates courses.html and bosses.html off for the beta (`showCoursesPage: false`, config.js:40) and cq-track.js is the telemetry client — a missed CACHE bump means returning testers keep the old gates and the old tracker, and the funnel data quietly goes stale.
fix: Keep ONE cache layer. At the HTTP layer, pin Cloudflare's current (correct) behaviour explicitly in website/_headers: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` in the `/*` block, plus `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` on `/sw.js` — the SW is the vehicle for every other fix and must never be held. Revalidation against Cloudflare's edge is a cheap 304, so the cost is one conditional request per asset, not a re-download. Do NOT add long max-age to /assets/, /finn/ or /bosses/ while filenames are unhashed; that is a second, uncoordinated pinning layer and it is how 'I deployed but my phone shows the old version' happens (a bug game.html:24145-24147 already documents fighting). Leave the SW's version-keyed cache as the only long-lived cache. One parser trap when writing the rules: Cloudflare 308s /play.html -> /play, so the 200 is issued for the CLEAN path — a rule scoped to `/*.html` would never match the page anyone actually loads. Scope cache rules to `/*` or list both forms.
maintainabilityCost: Zero added ritual — `must-revalidate` at HTTP is what already happens, and the SW CACHE bump is already the documented per-release step. The honest tradeoff of NOT adding long max-age: repeat visitors issue a conditional request per asset instead of hitting local cache silently. For a 10-20 tester beta with rapid builds that is unambiguously the right trade; revisit only if hashed filenames are ever introduced (which would require the build step that deliberately does not exist).

title: Compression is correct by default — the only actionable risk is trying to configure it
evidence: Nothing in the repo enables, disables or configures compression: no website/_headers, no _routes.json, no wrangler.toml. Cloudflare Pages applies Brotli/gzip automatically by content type. title: beta-ingest origin allowlist uses prefix matching — https://playchartquest.com.evil.com is accepted and echoed back
evidence: Both the repo copy and the DEPLOYED v3 (fetched via get_edge_function) contain `const isAllowed = ALLOWED_ORIGINS.some((o) => origin.startsWith(o));` and then `'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': isAllowed ? origin : ALLOWED_ORIGINS[0]`. The identical bug was found and fixed in the two sibling functions — deployed `ingest` v3 and `update-progress` v5 both now read `const ALLOWED_ORIGINS = new Set([...])` with the comment "It also used a prefix match, which would have accepted https://playchartquest.com.evil.com. Both fixed here." beta-ingest, the newest function and the one the closed beta actually depends on, never got that fix. Note the prefix list also includes bare `'http://localhost'`, which matches `http://localhost.attacker.com`.
risk: Any attacker-registered hostname beginning with the allowed prefix passes the check AND gets its own origin echoed in Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so a hostile page can write to beta_events/beta_surveys cross-origin from a real browser with real victim IPs. Caveat worth stating plainly: an Origin check is only ever a browser control — a script can send any Origin header it likes, so this allowlist stops nothing determined either way. The prefix bug matters because it converts a browser-enforced boundary into no boundary at all.

Severity should be Medium, not High (timing BEFORE_PUBLIC_BETA is correct). Four corrections to the finding as written:

1. RISK OVERSTATED. "it names no one who could sue, license, or be served" is legally wrong. Copyright vests on creation; the actual owner retains standing regardless of what the ToS says. The naming gap weakens contract formation and reads as untrustworthy — it does not extinguish enforcement rights.

2. PARTIAL MITIGATION OMITTED. website/game.html:3-6 already carries both a named holder and an explicit proprietary notice — "Copyright © 2024-2026 Dream Home Spotlight. All rights reserved." followed by "This source code is proprietary and confidential." Because there is no build step, that notice ships verbatim inside the 1.87 MB readable source a casual copier would take. The IP-protection risk is therefore materially lower than claimed.

3. THE FINDING UNDERSTATES THE REAL DEFECT. Focusing on the ownership clause misses the larger gap: grep -nE '"we"|refer to|means |We are ' over terms.html and privacy.html returns NOTHING. Both documents use "we"/"us" throughout ("We may suspend accounts that break these rules." terms.html:60; "we will delete it promptly." privacy.html:80) and never define who "we" is. An undefined counterparty is a bigger contract-formation problem than one vague ownership sentence, and it appears in the Children-and-families section that invites parents to contact an unnamed operator at a Gmail address.

They're real gameplay from an earlier build. To refresh them: capture the screens below on the **current build**, then hand them to me — I'll drop each into the **same filename**". Also line 24: "I frame them in fake \"browser/phone\" chrome on the site anyway."
risk: A public URL in the founder's own voice-of-the-team stating that the marketing screenshots are placeholders from an older build, and that the site frames them in "fake" chrome. The word "fake" next to "placeholders" is the exact pairing a sceptical tester or competitor would screenshot. It is also written in an AI assistant's first person ("hand them to me — I'll drop each into…"), which discloses how the site is produced. Nothing here is a security issue; it is purely a credibility one, and it is free to remove.
fix: Move the file out of the deploy path — /Users/owl/Claude/Projects/Shell Trade/docs/SCREENSHOTS.md — and delete website/assets/SCREENSHOTS.md. The content stays useful; it just stops being a public URL.
maintainabilityCost: None. It is documentation with no referrer; nothing loads it. Confirm no <link>/<a> points at it before moving (none found).

title: Dead-code canvas wordmarks render "CHART QUEST" as two words
evidence: Line 19612, inside drawCandleAcademy card 0: "ctx.fillText('CHART QUEST', cx, H * 0.68);" followed by "ctx.fillText('Learn crypto. One candle at a time.', cx, H * 0.74);". Line 21809, inside the opening cinematic's drawTitle(): "ctx.fillText('CHART QUEST', W / 2, H * 0.40);" then "ctx.fillText('LOST IN THE BLOCKCHAIN', W / 2, H * 0.40 + 28);". I verified BOTH are currently unreachable for a fresh player: candleAcademy is constructed active at line 6222 ("active: !localStorage.getItem('cq_played')") but the first-play branch immediately disables it at line 2016 — "candleAcademy.active = false;   // cinematic's title card replaces the greeting"; and the only route into drawTitle is setPhase('title') at 21087, reached solely from advanceValidator, whose phase is marked at 21244 "case 'validator':   // (retained but no longer entered — kept for safety)".
risk: No screenshot risk today — I confirmed neither path executes in the fresh-player flow, so I am NOT reporting these as live. The risk is latent and specific: both sit one boolean away from rendering. Re-enabling the Candle Academy greeting, or restoring the validator beat, would put a two-word wordmark full-screen on the game's title card — the most brand-critical pixel in the product. They also carry two more taglines ("Learn crypto. One candle at a time.", "LOST IN THE BLOCKCHAIN") that no longer match the shipped positioning, "The World's First Trading RPG".
fix: Change both string literals to 'CHARTQUEST' now, while they are inert and the edit carries zero regression risk. Decide separately whether the dead validator/academy paths should be deleted — that is a cleanup call, not a branding one, and deleting code in this file is riskier than editing two strings.
maintainabilityCost: None for the string change — two literals inside existing fillText calls, no layout or state touched. I am explicitly not recommending the dead-code deletion, which would be a real regression risk in a 28,000-line single file for no branding benefit.

title: Stale infrastructure hostnames and pre-rename storage keys in readable deployed source
evidence: Line 1727: "const _ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['chart-quest-game.netlify.app', 'localhost', '127.0.0.1', 'shelltrader.github.io'];" and 1728: "const _ALLOWED_HOST_SUFFIXES = ['--chart-quest-game.netlify.app'];" — the adjacent comment confirms these are inert: "(allowlist kept for reference / future analytics; it no longer blocks anything)". Legacy storage keys: 8136 "const JOURNAL_KEY = 'shellTradeJournal_v1';", 8380 "const NOTES_KEY = 'shellTradeNotes_v1';", 11955 "const DAILY_KEY = 'shellTradeDaily_v1';", with the reset path at 1686 matching both eras: "if (/^(cq_|shellTrade)/.test(k)) localStorage.removeItem(k);"
risk: Minor and mostly informational. The dead allowlist discloses two prior hosting identities (a Netlify site and the shelltrader GitHub org) in the readable source of the deployed game, which quietly confirms the project's former name to anyone reading. The storage keys surface the pre-rename name in DevTools → Application → Local Storage, where any technical tester will see "shellTradeJournal_v1" sitting under a product called ChartQuest. Neither leaks anything sensitive; both are brand-consistency papercuts.
fix: Delete the two dead allowlist constants at 1727-1728 (nothing reads them; the comment says so). DO NOT rename the three storage keys — see cost below.
maintainabilityCost: Deleting the allowlist: none, they are unreferenced. Renaming the storage keys: this is where I am recommending AGAINST the change. The keys hold the Trading Journal, Notes and Daily-streak state; renaming them either orphans every existing tester's journal and streak or requires a read-old/write-new migration path plus the reset regex at line 1686. That is exactly the save-data change the founder ruled out, and it buys only a cosmetic improvement in a DevTools panel. Leave them. If the naming ever genuinely matters, do it at a planned save-schema version bump, not as branding cleanup.

title: Unsubstantiated superlative "The World's First Trading RPG" in title, OG, Twitter and manifest
evidence: index.html:6 "<title>ChartQuest — The World's First Trading RPG</title>"; :82 "<meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"ChartQuest — The World's First Trading RPG\">"; :93 twitter:title identical; website/manifest.webmanifest "\"name\": \"ChartQuest — The World's First Trading RPG\"". Four occurrences, all consistent — this is a deliberate positioning line, not drift.
risk: "The World's First" is a factual, falsifiable claim rather than puffery, and trading/market RPGs and stock-market games predate this product. It sits in the PWA manifest name, so it also becomes the installed app's name on a tester's home screen. Low risk while the beta is closed and invited; it becomes an advertising-substantiation question at public launch, and it is the kind of claim a competitor points at. Flagging it because the founder has already run an overclaims pass (build 328) and this one survived — worth a conscious decision rather than an oversight.
fix: Founder's call, not an automatic fix. If he can substantiate it, keep it and be ready to. If not, a defensible alternative that keeps the punch: "ChartQuest — Learn to trade inside the chart" or "ChartQuest — The Trading RPG". Whatever is chosen, change all four places together so the brand line stays consistent.
maintainabilityCost: None. Four static strings. The only caution is to update the manifest name in the same commit and bump website/sw.js:19 CACHE, or installed testers keep the old name from cache.

title: Privacy and Terms pages have no footer, no copyright line and no navigation
evidence: grep for 'ChartQuest closed beta · playchartquest.com" — and only index.html:1512 carries a copyright line at all. privacy.html and terms.html end with a bare mailto: privacy.html:75 "emailing habitsimulator@gmail.com".
risk: The two legal documents are the pages a cautious tester or a parent (privacy.html:80 addresses them directly) will read most carefully, and they are the only pages with no brand footer, no copyright notice, no last-updated date and no way back to the site. That reads as boilerplate pasted in rather than a considered policy, which undercuts the trust those pages exist to build — and, per finding 2, they are also where the ownership claim should live.
fix: Add the survey.html footer pattern to privacy.html and terms.html, extended with the entity and a date: "© 2024-2026 Dream Home Spotlight · ChartQuest · playchartquest.com · Last updated 4 August 2026". This closes finding 2's copyright gap at the same time.
maintainabilityCost: None, with one ongoing habit: the "Last updated" date must be touched whenever the policy text changes. That is a normal obligation for a legal page, not new overhead. Do not use the auto-year JS from index.html:1581 here — a policy date must be the real revision date, not today's.
